title: Cardiac Arrest — Start CPR
info:
Confirm: no pulse, no normal breathing (agonal gasping only).

Start high-quality CPR immediately:
• Rate 100–120 compressions/min
• Depth ≥ 2 in (5 cm) in adults
• Allow full chest recoil between compressions
• Minimize interruptions (< 10 sec)

Give oxygen. Attach monitor/defibrillator as soon as available.

title: CPR × 2 min + IV/IO Access
info:

Establish IV or IO access.
Consider an advanced airway and waveform capnography if not already placed.

title: CPR × 2 min + Epinephrine
info:
Resume CPR immediately for 2 minutes.
Give Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO — repeat every 3–5 minutes for the remainder of the arrest.
Consider an advanced airway and capnography if not already placed.

title: CPR × 2 min + Antiarrhythmic
info:
Resume CPR for 2 minutes.
Give Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO (first dose) OR Lidocaine 1–1.5 mg/kg IV/IO (first dose).
Continue Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 minutes.

title: Identify & Treat Reversible Causes (H's and T's)
info:
H's:
• Hypovolemia
• Hypoxia
• Hydrogen ion (acidosis)
• Hypo-/Hyperkalemia
• Hypothermia

T's:
• Tension pneumothorax
• Tamponade, cardiac
• Toxins
• Thrombosis, pulmonary
• Thrombosis, coronary

title: Rhythm Check
question: Is the rhythm still shockable?
info: Continue 2-minute CPR / rhythm-check cycles, shocking and re-dosing epinephrine (every 3–5 min) until ROSC, rhythm changes, or resuscitation is terminated.

info:

title: Non-Shockable Rhythm — CPR + Epinephrine
info:
Continue high-quality CPR for 2 minutes.
Establish IV/IO access.
Give Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO as soon as possible — repeat every 3–5 minutes.
Consider an advanced airway and capnography.
Identify and treat reversible causes (H's and T's).

title: ROSC — Post-Cardiac Arrest Care
warning:
Cardiac Arrest Protocol Algorithm*
* From AHA/ACC and ESC updated guidelines/JCS adoption.
disposition:
Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) achieved.

Post-cardiac arrest care:
• Optimize ventilation/oxygenation (titrate SpO₂ ≥ 94%, avoid hyperventilation)
• Treat hypotension (IV/IO fluid bolus, vasopressor infusion)
• Obtain a 12-lead ECG
• Consider targeted temperature management if the patient remains comatose
• Identify and treat reversible causes
• Transport to an appropriate facility with continuous reassessment

title: Consider Termination of Resuscitation
warning:
Cardiac Arrest Protocol Algorithm*
* From AHA/ACC and ESC updated guidelines/JCS adoption.
disposition: Consider termination of resuscitation per local protocol, medical control, and clinical judgment (e.g., prolonged downtime, no reversible causes identified, advance directives). This decision should be made together with medical direction.
